title: Binomial probability mass function sums to one
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $p$ be a real number with $0 \le p \le 1$. Then the binomial probabilities $\binom{n}{k}\, p^k\, (1-p)^{n-k}$ sum to one over all outcomes, \[\sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k}\, p^k\, (1-p)^{n-k} = 1.\]
replaced:
If $0 \le p \le 1$, then the binomial PMF sums to $1$ over $k$ ranging in $\{0, \dots, n\}$,
i.e.\ $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \mathrm{binomialPMF}\,n\,p\,k = 1$. This is the binomial theorem
applied to $(p + (1-p))^n = 1$.
